enonce_markdown:
Combine the following two sentences into ONE sentence. Start your sentence with 'Although'.

1. The weather was cold.
2. The children played outside all afternoon.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode

« Although » (bien que) introduit toujours une proposition complète, avec un sujet et un verbe conjugué. On place la subordonnée en tête de phrase, suivie d'une virgule, puis la proposition principale.

### Corrigé

**Although the weather was cold, the children played outside all afternoon.**

'The weather was cold' is already a complete clause (subject + verb + complement), exactly what 'although' requires, so it can be used unchanged as the subordinate clause.

enonce_markdown:
Combine the following two sentences into ONE sentence. Start your sentence with 'Despite'.

1. There was heavy traffic.
2. We arrived at the airport on time.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode

« Despite » (malgré) est toujours suivi d'un nom ou d'un groupe nominal, jamais d'un sujet et d'un verbe conjugué. Contrairement à « in spite of », il n'est jamais suivi de « of ».

### Corrigé

**Despite the heavy traffic, we arrived at the airport on time.**

'There was heavy traffic' becomes the simple noun phrase 'the heavy traffic': 'despite' is followed directly by this noun phrase, with no 'of' and no conjugated verb.

enonce_markdown:
Combine the following two sentences into ONE sentence. Start your sentence with 'In spite of'. Remember: 'in spite of' must be followed by a noun, never by a full clause — so you will need to turn the adjective 'nervous' into a noun.

1. He was extremely nervous before the interview.
2. He answered every question calmly.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode

« In spite of » (comme « despite ») exige lui aussi un nom, jamais une proposition conjuguée. Quand la phrase de départ contient un adjectif, il faut le transformer en nom correspondant (nervous → nervousness) et adapter l'adverbe éventuel en adjectif (extremely → extreme).

### Corrigé

**In spite of his extreme nervousness before the interview, he answered every question calmly.**

The adjective 'nervous' becomes the noun 'nervousness', the adverb 'extremely' becomes the adjective 'extreme' to modify that noun, and the subject 'he' becomes the possessive 'his' — so that 'in spite of' is followed by a pure noun phrase, never by 'he was nervous'.

enonce_markdown:
Combine the following two sentences into ONE sentence. Start your sentence with 'Even though'.

1. She had never visited Paris before.
2. She found her way around the city easily.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode

« Even though » a le même sens que « although » mais insiste davantage sur le contraste. Il est lui aussi suivi d'une proposition complète, avec un sujet et un verbe conjugué, jamais d'un simple nom.

### Corrigé

**Even though she had never visited Paris before, she found her way around the city easily.**

'She had never visited Paris before' is a complete clause (subject + past perfect verb), which is exactly what 'even though' requires as its subordinate clause.

enonce_markdown:
Combine the following two sentences into ONE sentence. Start your sentence with 'No matter how'.

1. The road is very difficult.
2. The delivery team always finds a way to reach remote villages.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode

« No matter how » + adjectif (ou adverbe) + sujet + verbe exprime une concession portant sur un degré : « quel que soit le degré de… ». L'adjectif de la phrase de départ se place juste après « how », suivi du sujet puis du verbe.

### Corrigé

**No matter how difficult the road is, the delivery team always finds a way to reach remote villages.**

The adjective 'difficult' moves right after 'how', followed by the subject 'the road' and the verb 'is': this structure means 'whatever degree of difficulty the road has'.

enonce_markdown:
A classmate tried to combine two ideas using 'although', but made a mistake that many French-speaking learners make. Read the four versions given as answer choices below and choose the ONE that is grammatically correct in English.

Original ideas: The internet connection was very slow. / The students managed to finish the online test.
corrige_markdown:
### Rappel de méthode

En français, on peut dire « bien que… mais… », mais en anglais « although » (comme « even though ») introduit à lui seul l'opposition : on ne double jamais le connecteur avec « but ». Par ailleurs, « despite »/« in spite of » exigent un nom, jamais un sujet et un verbe conjugué.

### Corrigé

The correct sentence is **B) Although the internet connection was very slow, the students managed to finish the online test.**

- Option A repeats the idea of opposition twice ('although' ... 'but'), which is incorrect in English even though this mirrors the French 'bien que... mais...'. Only one connector is needed.
- Option C uses 'despite' followed by a full clause ('despite the internet connection was very slow'), but 'despite' can only be followed by a noun phrase, such as 'despite the very slow internet connection'.
- Option D drops the conjugated verb after 'although' ('the internet connection being very slow'), which is ungrammatical: a complete clause needs a conjugated verb ('was'), not an '-ing' form, especially since the subject of this clause is not the same as the subject of the main clause.
- Option B keeps a single connector ('although') followed by a complete clause ('the internet connection was very slow'), which is the correct structure.

choix.texte: Although the internet connection was very slow, but the students managed to finish the online test.
Although the internet connection was very slow, the students managed to finish the online test.
Despite the internet connection was very slow, the students managed to finish the online test.
Although the internet connection being very slow, the students managed to finish the online test.
